scope: Independent static review of CameraExtra and its final corrections. No product modifications, test build, or live action.

source.status: Final source fingerprint verified after reviewing both corrections.

verdict: Both reported guard/ownership findings are resolved. No remaining significant issue identified in the reviewed source. The queue phase, task identity and original forwarding match the inspected native path.

tests.reported_result: Author reports 604 checks, zero failures and no /W4 warnings. Reviewer read the relevant final fixture cases; no duplicate build was run.

findings.status: Resolved: CodeReady now checks all eight ControllerGetter bytes at164E70 before queueing and before dispatch
findings.Finding: CodeReady pins 430B40/430B60 and the two setters but omits their Controller getter 164E70. FreshLease checks static Controller718C60, while the native request wrappers obtain their target through this getter.
findings.impact: A changed getter can direct the validated setter to an object that FreshLease never checked.
findings.recommendation: Pin all eight getter bytes (48 8D 05 E9 3D 5B 00 C3), or call the checked pointer-argument setter directly with the validated Controller address.

findings.status: Resolved: all post-Original flag writes were removed; the native consumer owns subsequent flag state
findings.Finding: FollowFrame clears a still-equal request byte after Original. Equality alone cannot distinguish an unconsumed trainer request from a request consumed and then replaced by native or modded code during the call.
findings.impact: The cleanup can erase a later writer's equal-valued request. The inspected unmodified consumer already clears these bytes synchronously.
findings.recommendation: Avoid the post-call restore based only on equality, or provide a stronger observed ownership guarantee. Add a synthetic test that Original consumes the trainer flag and then sets a new request.

verified: FreshLease requires thread, host, scene, owner0, submode0, bank0 and single-camera context; it resolves the current player/status pair and checks follow actor identity and actor controller readability.
Queued requests retain scheduler, heap, player, status, actor-controller identity and all10MapTargetbytes. Timeout is1500ms; lost conditions cancel without first writing an engine flag.
Installation scans the complete bounded scheduler list and rejects wrong owners, backlinks, ordering, tail, duplicate matching tasks and continuation/fiber nodes.
Hook mutation uses compare-exchange from exact original to own wrapper or own wrapper to exact original. It does not replace an observed foreign callback.
CurrentTask requires manager+32 to be the executing node, owner/group/priority/continuation/function identity, matching the intended native follow phase.
BeforeFollow requires both native flags to be clear and calls only one request immediately before Original. The pending trainer request is removed before dispatch.
Original follow callback is invoked once after normal preparation or caught preparation faults. The unmodified follow body checks owner0 and consumes recenter+65 or snap+64 in that same call.
Roll action240 uses the independently reviewed World API; it changes trainer-held radians and waits for the normal renderer phase.
Reset discards pending trainer requests and attempts only own callback restoration in the current fresh scheduler. The resident wrapper remains a forwarding path when no request exists.
test_recommendations: Changed getter bytes reject before native setter invocation.
Whole-list malformed links, duplicate candidate, busy manager, foreign hook and CAS race preserve foreign state.
Lost host/scene/actor/heap/map/owner/submode after queuing results in no native request.
CurrentTask with manager+32 mismatch cancels; Original still exactly once.
Original consumes request; post-call code must preserve a new equal-valued request created after consumption.
Disable before callback clears only pending trainer state; no stale native request later.
limitations: This verdict applies to the recorded final source and test fingerprints.
No synthetic execution or live behavior was tested by this reviewer.
The normal consumer is synchronous in inspected native code; unknown mods may alter deeper calls.
